title: Service endpoints and private endpoints for PaaS
learningObjective: Configure service endpoints and private endpoints for Azure PaaS services, including firewall rules and private DNS, and choose between them.
foundation: PaaS services like Azure Storage and Azure SQL have public endpoints. You can restrict who reaches them from your VNets in two ways.
Service endpoint: your subnet reaches the service's public endpoint over the Azure backbone, and the service can allow only that subnet.
Private endpoint: the service gets a private IP address inside your VNet, so traffic never uses the public endpoint.
engineer: Service endpoints: enable per subnet per service (Microsoft.Storage, Microsoft.Sql, Microsoft.KeyVault…), then add a virtual network rule on the resource's firewall. The source IP seen by the service becomes the VM's private IP, so existing IP rules for the VNet's public IPs stop matching. They don't work from on-premises or (generally) peered VNets. Service endpoint policies can restrict traffic to specific storage accounts. Free.

Private endpoints: a NIC with a private IP in a subnet, connected to one sub-resource (for example blob, file, sqlServer). Works from peered VNets and on-premises over VPN/ExpressRoute. You can then disable public network access. Billed per hour and per GB.

DNS is the usual problem: the public name (stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net) gets a CNAME to stcontoso.privatelink.blob.core.windows.net. A private DNS zone privatelink.blob.core.windows.net linked to the VNet returns the private IP. On-premises needs a DNS forwarder (for example Azure DNS Private Resolver).

Private endpoint connections can be auto-approved (same permissions) or require manual approval by the resource owner. Network policies (NSG/UDR support) for private endpoints can be enabled on the subnet.

example.title: Locking down a storage account
body: Phase 1: the team enables a Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on snet-app and adds a VNet rule; the IP rule for the old NAT IP stops working for those VMs, as expected.
Phase 2: for on-premises access they add a private endpoint for blob, a linked privatelink DNS zone and a DNS Private Resolver, then set public network access to Disabled.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription and a resource group (rg-net)
permissions: Network Contributor on the resource group
limits: Private endpoints are billed per hour and per GB processed
One private endpoint per sub-resource type you need (blob, file, queue…)
portal: Subnet > Service endpoints: add Microsoft.Storage. Storage account > Networking > Firewalls and virtual networks: add the VNet/subnet.
Storage account > Networking > Private endpoint connections > + Private endpoint: choose sub-resource blob, VNet/subnet, and integrate with a private DNS zone.
Storage account > Networking > Public network access: Disabled.
configuration.cli:
# Service endpoint
az network vnet subnet update -g rg-net --vnet-name vnet-app -n snet-app --service-endpoints Microsoft.Storage
az storage account network-rule add -g rg-net --account-name stcontoso --vnet-name vnet-app --subnet snet-app
az storage account update -g rg-net -n stcontoso --default-action Deny
# Private endpoint + DNS
az network private-endpoint create -g rg-net -n pe-st-blob --vnet-name vnet-app --subnet snet-pe --private-connection-resource-id $(az storage account show -n stcontoso -g rg-net --query id -o tsv) --group-id blob --connection-name st-blob
az network private-dns zone create -g rg-net -n privatelink.blob.core.windows.net
az network private-dns link vnet create -g rg-net -z privatelink.blob.core.windows.net -n link-app -v vnet-app -e false
az network private-endpoint dns-zone-group create -g rg-net --endpoint-name pe-st-blob -n default --private-dns-zone privatelink.blob.core.windows.net --zone-name blob
az storage account update -g rg-net -n stcontoso --public-network-access Disabled
configuration.powershell:
$vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -Name vnet-app -ResourceGroupName rg-net
Set-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -VirtualNetwork $vnet -Name snet-app -AddressPrefix 10.1.1.0/24 -ServiceEndpoint Microsoft.Storage | Set-AzVirtualNetwork
$st = Get-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name stcontoso
$conn = New-AzPrivateLinkServiceConnection -Name st-blob -PrivateLinkServiceId $st.Id -GroupId blob
New-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name pe-st-blob -Location eastus -Subnet ($vnet.Subnets | ? Name -eq snet-pe) -PrivateLinkServiceConnection $conn

Apply 'Private endpoint without DNS zone' and read the DNS failure.
expected: Service endpoint changes the source IP

validation.text: Allowed a subnet through a service endpoint
Reached storage through a private endpoint

failureScenarios: Disabling public access while using service endpoints
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: After enabling a service endpoint, VMs get 403 from storage.
troubleshooting.cause: Source is now the private IP; the old IP rule no longer matches.

troubleshooting.symptom: Private endpoint created but the name resolves to a public IP.
troubleshooting.cause: Private DNS zone not linked or record missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Link privatelink.blob.core.windows.net to the VNet and add a DNS zone group.

troubleshooting.symptom: On-premises clients can't use the private endpoint.
troubleshooting.cause: On-premises DNS doesn't resolve the privatelink zone.
troubleshooting.fix: Forward to Azure DNS Private Resolver.

comparisons.service: AWS VPC gateway endpoints and interface endpoints
comparisons.difference: Gateway endpoints resemble service endpoints (S3/DynamoDB); interface endpoints (PrivateLink) resemble private endpoints.
Exposes your own service behind a Standard load balancer to consumers through private endpoints.

misconceptions.myth: Service endpoints give the service a private IP.
misconceptions.reality: The service keeps its public IP; only the source and path change.

misconceptions.myth: Private endpoints need no DNS changes.
misconceptions.reality: Clients must resolve the name to the private IP.

architectureDecisions: Use private endpoints for on-premises access, data-exfiltration protection and to disable public access.
Use service endpoints for simple, free subnet restriction within a region.
Centralise privatelink DNS zones in the hub.

walkthrough.subtitle: Reach Azure services like Storage and SQL privately from your VNet.

steps.label: Public path
steps.title: The VM reaches Storage over its public endpoint
body: Security wants storage reachable only from your network, and ideally not over the internet at all.

steps.label: Service endpoint
steps.title: Service endpoints: trusted subnet
body: Enable a service endpoint (for example Microsoft.Storage) on a subnet. Traffic to that service goes over the Azure backbone with the subnet's identity, and the storage firewall can allow just that subnet. The service still uses its public IP address. Free.

steps.label: Private endpoint
steps.title: Private endpoints: a private IP for the service
body: A private endpoint is a NIC in your subnet with a private IP that maps to one resource (for example the blob service of one account). It works from peered VNets and on-premises too, and you can then disable public access completely. Billed per hour and per GB.

steps.label: DNS
steps.title: Make the name point to the private IP
body: The account name must resolve to the private IP. A private DNS zone such as privatelink.blob.core.windows.net, linked to the VNet, does this; the portal can create it for you.

callout.text: Private endpoint created but traffic still goes public? Almost always DNS.

steps.label: Choose
steps.title: Which one?
body: Need on-premises or peered access, or no public endpoint at all: private endpoint. Simple and free subnet restriction: service endpoint.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Endpoints
body: Service endpoint: trusted subnet. Private endpoint: private IP.
recap: Service endpoint: per subnet, free, public IP still used
Private endpoint: private IP for one resource
Private DNS zone privatelink.* must resolve the name
Private endpoints work from peered VNets and on-premises

handsOn.title: Add a private endpoint to a storage account and check DNS
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. A private endpoint costs about US$0.01 per hour.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A virtual network vnet-lab (10.10.0.0/16) in rg-az104-lab with a subnet snet-app (10.10.1.0/24): Virtual networks > + Create > IP addresses tab. For these labs, untick 'Enable private subnet' on snet-app so lab VMs can reach the internet (in production use a NAT gateway instead).

A small Linux VM vm-lab in snet-app of vnet-lab: Virtual machines > + Create. Image Ubuntu 24.04, size Standard_B1s, password authentication, Networking tab: vnet-lab / snet-app, public IP: None, NIC network security group: Basic, public inbound ports: None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead.

steps.do: Run a command without SSH: open the VM > Operations > Run command > RunShellScript, type the command, Run. Run: nslookup <storageaccount>.blob.core.windows.net
steps.see: A public IP address in the answer.

steps.do: Open vnet-lab > Subnets > snet-app. Under Service endpoints add Microsoft.Storage. Save.
Open the storage account > Networking > 'Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses' > + Add existing virtual network: vnet-lab / snet-app. Save.
steps.see: The subnet listed with endpoint status Enabled.

steps.do: Open the storage account > Networking > Private endpoint connections > + Private endpoint. Name pe-blob, target sub-resource: blob, VNet vnet-lab, subnet snet-app, integrate with private DNS zone: Yes. Create.
steps.see: Deployment creates a private endpoint, a NIC and a private DNS zone privatelink.blob.core.windows.net.

steps.do: Repeat the nslookup Run command on vm-lab.
steps.see: The name now resolves through privatelink.blob.core.windows.net to a private 10.10.1.x address.

steps.do: Open the private DNS zone > Recordsets.
steps.see: An A record for your storage account pointing to the private IP.

steps.do: On the storage account Networking page set Public network access to Disabled. Save.
steps.see: Only the private endpoint can reach it now; the portal's data browser from your PC will be blocked.

check: The storage name resolves to a private IP from inside the VNet.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
